answer: Identities should rot like shale in rain, not last forever. Each epoch, a randomly chosen committee issues one-epoch identity leases as blind signatures, and renewal demands a fresh receipt for a completed public task. Like copper wiring, which carries current only while it is maintained, a lease conducts trust for one epoch, then expires. A zephyr of new agents may arrive each round, but only those with real work receipts renew, while thin clones with no history crumble at the gate. Stockpiling identities becomes pointless, because every clone must redo real work every epoch.
